tasks.title: The SHARED capture rig catches RuntimeException, not Throwable — so 'N asked / N observed / 0 errored' cannot distinguish 'none errored' from 'none asked that errors'
tasks.description: RAISED BY T159, WHICH FOUND IT BY DETONATING IT rather than by reading. The shared Java capture rig -- inherited by T83, T84, T100 AND T117 alike -- catches RuntimeException, not Throwable. A java.lang.StackOverflowError is an Error, NOT a RuntimeException, so it is precisely what slips through, AND T159 OBSERVED EXACTLY THAT: two cells died with java.lang.StackOverflowError from ProgressiveEMICalculator.calculateLastUnpaidRepaymentPeriodEMI recursing into itself at ProgressiveEMICalculator.java:1214, non-monotonically -- (B=10001,n=2000) dies while (B=10001,n=3000) succeeds. WHY THIS IS A MEASUREMENT DEFECT AND NOT A ROBUSTNESS NIT: every sweep this program has run reports an integrity line of the form 'N asked / N observed / 0 errored / 0 skipped', and that line is cited as PROOF THE SWEEP IS COMPLETE. With this hole, '0 errored' is consistent with BOTH 'nothing failed' AND 'the failures were invisible to the handler' -- the P-40 class (an enumerator that cannot see what it skipped) reaching the ERROR path instead of the enumeration path. Fix: catch Throwable, record the throwable's class and message as a FIRST-CLASS OUTCOME distinct from both success and absence, and make the integrity line report it -- 'N asked / N observed / N threw / N skipped'. tasks.title: G-12 — Fineract STORES a running balance on the journal entry; our non-negotiable says balances are DERIVED, never written
tasks.description: RAISED BY A2-26 FROM A DB DUMP, local fire 20260822-000013. acc_gl_journal_entry carries office_running_balance and organization_running_balance -- Fineract STORES A BALANCE ON THE ENTRY. CLAUDE.md's non-negotiable is 'The ledger is double-entry and append-only. Balances are derived, NEVER WRITTEN.' So the reference oracle does the thing the port is forbidden to do. This is the SAME SHAPE AS G-8 -- 'Fineract is the oracle' set against a stated invariant -- and G-8's handling is the precedent: measure the boundary first, then choose, and note that options which narrow the graded domain are HARD USER GATES. MEASURE BEFORE RECOMMENDING. (a) Are those columns ever READ to serve a balance, or only written? Find every reader in the pinned checkout at 426a23544 and cite it. (b) Are they part of any CONTRACT-BOUNDARY response, or purely internal? A2-26 found them in a psql dump -- check whether /journalentries or any report surfaces them. (c) Does the value ever DISAGREE with the derived sum, and can you make it disagree? A stored balance that always equals the derived one is a CACHE; one that can drift is a second source of truth, and the two cases have completely different consequences for the port. This is the measurement that decides the gate -- do not skip it because it is the hard one. THEN raise the gate properly in .softhouse/gates.md with options and a recommendation, and update the GATE REGISTER TABLE AT THE TOP, which is authoritative when a section heading and the table disagree. Options to consider, not a closed list: (a) the port derives balances and simply does not populate the columns, accepting a schema-level divergence that no contract-boundary cell exposes; (b) the port writes them to keep the adopted PostgreSQL schema byte-compatible for shadow-parity, while NEVER READING them -- which honours 'derived' in behaviour and 'schema-first' in storage; (c) treat any vector cell that exposes them as outside the graded domain -- WHICH NARROWS THE GRADED DOMAIN AND IS THEREFORE A HARD USER GATE you may recommend but not take. NOTE THE ADOPTED-SCHEMA TENSION EXPLICITLY: CLAUDE.md says 'adopt Fineract's PostgreSQL schema' AND says balances are never written. Those two instructions meet in this column. Say so plainly rather than resolving it silently in one direction. You are NOT authorised to change a non-negotiable or the graded domain.
